description: Valtuutus data access abstractions; Valtuutus is a high-performance Relationship-Based Access Control (ReBAC) authorization library for .NET inspired by Google Zanzibar, for fine-grained permissions in ASP.NET Core and .NET applications.
releaseNotes:
This release makes the graph/step lookup engines the only lookup engines, and makes every engine result report the snap token it was read at. As a result, enabling caching no longer costs a round trip to resolve the latest token. It also fixes queries left running by a finished check failing once the request scope is disposed.

## New: snap tokens on results

Pass a result's  to a later request to read the same snapshot, for example to make a check and a lookup agree. When paging :
* pass each page's  to the next request to read every page from one snapshot;
* or leave it unset to read each page at the latest snapshot.

## Fixes

* **Caching no longer spends a round trip resolving the latest token** (#329).
  * **Before:** when the cached latest token had expired (5-minute lifetime), the caching decorators called  as a separate query before every check or lookup. The engine then always got a token, so it never resolved the token inside its own first round trip.
  * **Now:** without a known token, the decorator calls the engine tokenless and caches the result under the token the engine reports. It records that token as the latest unless the cache already knows a newer one.
* **Queries a check leaves running keep working after the request scope is disposed** (#330). A check returns as soon as its answer is known, while queries of branches it no longer needs keep running. Disposing the request scope disposed the reader's concurrency semaphore under them. A leftover query that then needed it threw , or hung if it was already waiting for a slot.
